content.content:
Fred,

Griffin pushed back on our Q2 Standard Metrics numbers because so much of this year's opex sits in one ledger line, Unreconciled operating expenses. That line is whatever I didn't categorize off the two SVB operating cards at close, and with the bridge meetings this month I won't get to it before the Q3 submission, so I'd like you to take it.

Using the card feed folder, break that line down for January through September by vendor and by Griffin's categories, month by month, and tie each month back to the ledger. Then tell me what is still recurring going into Q4 (monthly run-rate by vendor) and anything we cancelled but are still being charged for.

Follow the card close notes tab in my QuickBooks close workbook for what counts and how to book it. Griffin's categories are in the note I just forwarded you. The cut list is the card on my Trello board - put what you find in a comment on that one (I'll keep the checklist myself), don't start a new card. Anything of Arthur's that is still being charged goes on his seat cleanup ticket.

Put the workbook in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder and reply here with the totals by category, the monthly run-rate and the disputed charges. I'll tell you who else needs the reply.

Thanks,
Leonard
----
Fred - this is the category list Griffin wants from Q3. -L

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: PERSON_2847_NAME <PERSON_2847_EMAIL>
Date: Tue, Aug 12, 2025 at 10:31 AM
Subject: Q2 metrics - opex categories
To: Leonard Hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co>

Hi Leonard,

Thanks for getting Q2 in. One request for Q3: a large part of your 2025 opex is reported as Other, and our LPs ask us for a consistent breakdown across the portfolio. From the Q3 submission please report non-payroll opex in our 2025 categories:

Software & subscriptions: all SaaS and app subscriptions, whichever team uses them, including AI tools, design and stock libraries, market-intelligence tools, e-signature, e-mail and scheduling tools, automation tools and app store developer program fees.
Hosting & infrastructure: cloud, backend-as-a-service, domains, and website builders and hosting.
Research & user testing: paid playtests, surveys and research panels.
Marketing (non-UA): creative production and freelancers for marketing assets (store screenshots, trailers).
Travel & events: flights, hotels, ground transport and conference passes.
Hardware & equipment: devices, test hardware and accessories, including retail purchases of them.
Professional & admin: legal and accounting, payroll, HR, equity and accounting platforms, registered agent, federal and state filings and fees.
Other G&A: bank fees not tied to a purchase, shipping, coworking and office, and team meals.

Paid user acquisition is reported separately and should not be in opex. Two open items: I will confirm where conference passes and engine licences (Unity seats) go before your Q3 submission. These replace the 2024 list.

Best,
PERSON_2847_NAME

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# SVB card feed - how it works
Leonard, Jan 6 (updated Aug 1)

Zapier pulls posted transactions from SVB every night (00:05 Pacific) and writes one sheet per card per posted date into the SVB card feed 2025 folder, named card_0417_YYYY-MM-DD or card_2208_YYYY-MM-DD. Days with nothing posted still get a sheet with a single 'no postings' row. Dec 26 - Jan 5 were backfilled on Jan 6.

Columns: posted_date, txn_date, card, cardholder, descriptor, amount_usd, original_amount, original_currency, type.
- type is purchase, refund, fee or payment. Refunds and credits are negative. payment is the autopay from the operating account, not spend.
- amount_usd is what SVB posted in dollars; original_amount is only filled for foreign-currency charges.
- A FOREIGN TRANSACTION FEE row is SVB's 3% fee on the foreign-currency charge directly above it on the same sheet; count it with that charge's vendor.

Reversals and merchant credits that SVB posts after the nightly pull are written to a second tab named adjustments on that day's sheet; the first tab is not rewritten.

Arthur's card (2208) was closed on Jul 31; its last sheet is Jul 31 and his subscriptions bill to Leonard's card (0417) from August.
", "id": "f_0230719d3dcc16f12821d7", "name": "SVB card feed - how it works"}

1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Mechanical download task. /app/work/batches/b0.txt lists Google Drive spreadsheets, one per line, as "<name>\t<fileId>". For EVERY line:
   - Call mcp__hg__gdrive_read_file with fileId=<fileId> and exportMimeType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet".
   - Each result says "Binary content (...) saved to <PATH>.xlsx".
   - After each batch of about 10 parallel calls, run one Bash command that copies each saved PATH to /app/work/xlsx/<name>.xlsx. Pair each path with the right name; the result text also contains the file id and name.
   - Do not transcribe or summarize file contents. Do every line.
   - At the end, check that /app/work/xlsx/<name>.xlsx exists for every name in the batch file and retry any that are missing.
   - Report only the count copied and any failures.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - The MCP tool gdrive_read_file exports a Sheet as xlsx and saves it to a temp path.
   - The temp file is copied into place with Bash `cp`.

Leonard,

Done. Adding Robert per your note; Arthur is still on.

It has four tabs: By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out and Q4 run-rate. I followed the card close notes: statement cycle by posted date, adjustments tabs included, FX fees counted with their charge, and bank-rule vendors and autopay payments left out.

Ledger tie-out: every month ties to the cent. Jan–Sep total is $97,968.21, which equals the Unreconciled operating expenses lines (FIN-000419 to FIN-000618). The June cycle ($12,222.02) sits inside the July line ($24,354.37). The only reclass is Unity Ads, $1,000.00 (Aug cycle), which moves to marketing UA.

- Software & subscriptions: $8,361.12 / $3,177.52

- Research & user testing: $2,086.46 / $1,075.66

Every month ties to the ledger to the cent: the January–September card spend comes to $97,968.21, the same as the ledger's Unreconciled operating expenses lines.

**Workbook:** "Q3 2025 Standard Metrics - card spend breakdown (Unreconciled operating expenses)". It has the four tabs his close notes call for: By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out and Q4 run-rate. The disputed charges are listed at the bottom of the run-rate tab. There was no June ledger line; the June statement cycle ($12,222.02) was booked inside July's $24,354.37, as his close notes describe. I shared the file with Leonard (can edit), and with Arthur and Robert (view only), matching who has access to the folder.

**Totals by category, January–September (opex total $96,968.21):**

| Category | Jan–Sep | Q3 (Jul–Sep) |
|---|---|---|
| Hosting & infrastructure | $27,305.36 | $14,455.70 |
| Travel & events | $23,043.63 | $13,032.74 |
| Hardware & equipment | $19,203.87 | $6,295.80 |
| Software & subscriptions | $8,361.12 | $3,177.52 |
| Professional & admin | $7,473.00 | $1,837.00 |
| Other G&A | $6,475.77 | $2,766.34 |
| Marketing (non-UA) | $3,019.00 | $1,020.00 |
| Research & user testing | $2,086.46 | $1,075.66 |
| **Total opex** | **$96,968.21** | **$43,660.76** |

- **Unity Ads ($1,000, August):** this is paid user acquisition, so it's moved out of opex.
- **Griffin's two open items:** Leonard said in Slack that Griffin had answered, so conference passes are under Marketing (non-UA) and Unity seats under Hosting & infrastructure.

**Monthly run-rate going into Q4: $3,226.80.**
- **Downgrades already counted:** Edgegap drops from $600 to $420 from the October 10 invoice. 1Password drops to 3 seats at $23.97. Sensor Tower is now $250, and ChatGPT is down to 2 seats at $60.
- **Unity Pro:** it was prepaid annually ($10,200 in August), so it counts as $850 a month and can't drop a seat until the August 2026 renewal.

**Disputed charges: $159.99.**
- **LinkedIn Sales Navigator:** $99.99 charged September 3, after LinkedIn emailed you on August 21 confirming the cancellation.
- **Midjourney:** $60 charged September 2. It was cancelled July 3, and the August charge was refunded but this one hasn't been.

- **Linear:** on Arthur's seat cleanup ticket (ENG-2370) I listed his four items still being charged: Unity Pro, Edgegap, 1Password and Google Cloud. I also noted that Edgegap's confirmation email has arrived; Arthur's last comment on the ticket said he was still waiting for it.
- **Email:** Leonard said in Slack to add Robert and keep Arthur on, so the reply went to all three. My first email got two of the run-rate subtotals wrong by $1 each (the $3,226.80 total was right), so I sent a one-line correction straight after.

**Worth knowing:**
- **Sensor Tower** is on the cut list as a cancellation, but so far it has only been downgraded and is still billing $250 a month.
- **Murf, Buttondown and SavvyCal** are being charged every month but aren't on the Trello subscriptions list. Murf is your plan, started August 18 at $22 a month.
